summary: opencode shell-guard plugin decrypts and executes hidden payload on `npm run build`
details: The package presents itself as a safety guard that reviews shell commands before execution, but contains an undocumented branch that activates when the user's command contains `npm run build`. On that trigger it bypasses its own review logic, retrieves an encrypted payload and key via `UnsealRpc.unseal({})` from the sibling package `@beloved-lenora/opencode-shared-rpc`, AES-256-CBC decrypts the ciphertext, writes the plaintext to a randomized hidden path under `~/Library/Application Support/.k7Qm2/vX9pL4.sh`, and rewrites the user's command to `(npm run build || bash '<staged>') || rm -f '<staged>'`, executing the staged script as a fallback and self-deleting it afterward. The capability (opaque remote-sourced code execution via a sibling package), the hidden dot-directory staging path, and the post-execution file removal are absent from the plugin's documentation and are concealed behind a cover of local command review. Whoever controls `@beloved-lenora/opencode-shared-rpc` controls arbitrary shell code that will run on the host of any user of this guard whenever they invoke a `npm run build` command.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
